key_insight: Pressure can be treated as a geometric potential that curves an effective space, linking fluid motion, the pressure Poisson equation, and vortex identification through the same geometric framework.
engineering_relevance: This offers a unifying way to interpret turbulence diagnostics and may help design more physically grounded vortex-capture and flow-analysis methods, especially for 2D turbulence.
method: Build a Newton-Cartan geometric model for the flow.
Apply a conformal transformation to the spatial metric so pressure becomes effective curvature.
Interpret vortex-identification criteria as geometric invariants/projections of the resulting curvature tensor.
evidence_signal: The abstract presents a theoretical derivation showing that the Euler equation and pressure Poisson equation emerge from geodesic motion plus the Bianchi identity, with a special 2D result where the effective tensor and global curvature integral vanish.
watch_item: This is a theoretical framework; practical value will depend on how robustly the geometric quantities can be computed from noisy experimental or simulation data.
paper_title: On the relationships between pressure geometrization and vortex identification
